Pecan AI is a predictive analytics platform powered by Predictive GenAI (fusion of generative AI and machine learning). Website: pecan.ai. Contact: sales@pecan.ai. Founded 2018. Headquarters: Israel-based with global operations. Total funding raised: $117 million. Investors: Insight Partners, Google Ventures (GV), S Capital, Dell Technologies Capital. Primary tagline: 'Predictive AI for the people making decisions.' Supporting tagline: 'If you can read this, you can build a model.' CTA: 'Ask a question. Get a prediction. Act with confidence.' Mission: making AI-powered predictions accessible to all data and business teams by automating model creation and training. Client base: approximately 100 managed services customers. Platform is 'impacting billions of dollars in revenue' across client base. Leadership: Zohar Bronfman (CEO/Co-founder, two PhDs from Tel Aviv University), Noam Brezis (CTO/Co-founder, PhD in computational neuroscience), Yehonathan Barnea (VP Customer Success, prior AI leadership at DataRobot, MBA from MIT Sloan), Tomer Meron (VP R&D, 20+ years at eBay and Google).

Pecan core technology: Predictive AI Agent (launched January 2026, described as world's first Predictive AI Agent) -- understands data automatically, defines business question, prepares data, builds and validates model, delivers predictions without manual workflows or data science dependency. Predictive Chat/AI Co-Pilot -- natural language interface to translate business problem into predictive question, enables users to build first model within a day of signing up. Predictive Notebook -- auto-generated SQL creating training datasets, joins data tables from different sources, AI assistant helps adjust queries. AutoML Pipeline: automated data preparation (cleansing, outlier handling, missing data imputation), automated feature engineering and selection (evaluating dozens to hundreds of features), automated model building and selection (training 15-20 models and selecting best performer), automated MLOps (continuous monitoring, performance alerts, model retraining). Key technical claims: models built and trained within hours instead of weeks or months, zero coding knowledge required, 90% of predictions delivered without data science support, handles messy real-world data, no PII ever required or requested.

Pecan solutions: Customer Churn Prediction -- detects 85% of would-be churn, helps lower churn by roughly 15-20%, 12% average reduction in customer churn. Customer Lifetime Value (LTV/pLTV) -- predicts future value as early as 3 days after first transaction, 15% improvement in marketing ROAS. Demand Forecasting -- 25% reduction in inventory costs, requires 2+ years historical data preferred. Upsell and Cross-Sell -- predicts who will buy again and when. Customer Winback -- identifies which lapsed customers are most likely to re-engage. Fraud and Chargeback Prevention -- scores transactions for fraud risk, reduces false positives. Predictive Campaign ROAS -- forecasts ROAS 24-48 hours after launch, one mobile app customer achieved 279% lift in conversion and 64% lift in sales using predictive events on Facebook vs value optimization. Lead Scoring -- prioritizes leads with highest likelihood to convert. Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) -- measures multi-channel marketing impact, one major US company identified $100M+ in overspending and $200M+ in potential savings. iOS SKAdNetwork Optimization. Pricing Strategy (Nanit developed full pricing strategy in three weeks using Pecan).

Pecan ICP: Company type: B2C companies. Revenue size: ideally $10M-$500M. Employee count: 50-500 employees (subscription/SaaS models). Priority verticals: E-commerce (Shopify, BigCommerce brands), Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), Mobile apps (fitness, wellness, gaming), Subscription models (meal kits, subscription SaaS). Buying signals/tech stack: companies using Google Ads, Meta/Facebook Ads, TikTok Ads, Criteo, RTB House, Braze, Iterable, Klaviyo, Segment. Companies using Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL, IBM Db2, Amazon S3. Target titles: Analytics (CDO, CAO, VP of Analytics, VP of BI, Director of Analytics, Director of BI, Head of Data and Insights), Marketing (CMO, VP of Marketing, Director of Marketing, VP of Growth, Director of Growth), Revenue (CRO, VP of Revenue, VP of Sales and Marketing, Director of RevOps), Customer (VP of CX, Director of CX, CCO, VP of Customer Retention, VP of Customer Success). Qualifying questions: What data warehouse do you use? Do you have 2+ years historical data? What are you doing currently to predict churn/optimize campaign spend? Do you have a data science team? What is your biggest frustration with current analytics tools?

Pecan core differentiators: No data science team required (empowers analysts and business teams). Speed to value (first model within a day, hours not weeks/months, ROI within first quarter). Conversational AI interface (Predictive Agent and Predictive Chat, natural language). Full automation end-to-end (data prep, feature engineering, model building, selection, deployment, monitoring, retraining). Handles messy data explicitly (prefers messy real-world data). Continuous model maintenance (retrains as needed, ongoing partnership). Transparent and explainable (plain business terms, shows which factors drove predictions). Privacy by design (no PII ever required, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR ready). Affordable vs hiring data scientists (starts at $760/month vs $200K+ total comp for data scientist). Named competitors: Amazon SageMaker, Google Vertex AI -- Pecan positions as far simpler, faster, designed for business users not ML engineers. Key positioning: 'Copilots summarize. Pecan predicts.'

Pecan named clients: Kenvue (Johnson and Johnson consumer health), Johnson and Johnson, Mars, Nestlé, SciPlay, Redis, Little Spoon, Nanit, Wild Alaskan, Whistle Express Car Wash, Clearwave Fiber, TJC (The Jewelry Channel), The Credit Pros, Proper Cloth, Fiverr, BMC, CableOne, BlueTriton, Markel, Nucor, Food for the Poor, Hydrant, LivePerson, Ideal Image, CAA Club Group, Coinmama, Nexters, Dream. Key testimonials: Little Spoon (Adam Smith, Director of Strategic Analytics) -- 'predicts orders and inventory weeks ahead, turning subscription data into clear actionable forecasts.' Nanit (Amir Baruch, Senior Director of Data Analytics) -- 'developed full pricing strategy in three weeks, would have taken more than double without Pecan.' TJC (Ashish Dawra, VP of Global IT) -- 'started saving money on delivery grouping and reduced fraud percentage, translating into real business numbers.' Redis (Pnina Klein, VP of Data) -- 'truly a complete solution designed for analysts.' Kenvue (Neil Ackerman, Head of Worldwide Innovation) -- described Pecan's Predictive GenAI framework as 'a game changer.' Quantified results: 10-30% improvement in selected KPIs, 279% conversion lift and 64% sales lift for mobile app customer, $100M+ overspending identified/$200M+ savings for major US company using MMM, 140 hours per month manual effort reduced at Coinmama, 12% average churn reduction, 15% ROAS improvement, 25% inventory cost reduction.

Pecan pricing: Self-service plans (annual billing): Starter $760/month (2 prediction batches, 500M rows, 1 user), Team $1,400/month (10 batches, 2B rows, 3 users), Business $2,000/month (60 batches, 5B rows, 7 users), Enterprise custom. All plans commitment-free, cancel anytime, 20% annual billing discount. Extra prediction batch $50 per batch on all tiers. Managed services pricing: LTV/Lead Scoring starts at $6,000-$8,000 per month. MMM (first model, one geo) starts at $8,000 per month. Pricing per use case (one predictive question). Key pricing talking points: far less than a single data scientist salary (median $164,500 base, likely $200K+ total comp). No hidden costs. Commitment-free. ROI within first quarter.

Pecan security: ISO 27001 certified. SOC 2 Type II audit confirmed. GDPR ready. Data encrypted in transit and at rest. No PII ever required or requested ('Private and secure by design -- no PII required'). Every customer's information is siloed. User controls what data is shared. Partnerships with multinationals and insurance companies with no information security incidents reported. Rigid internal compartmentalization. Advanced endpoint and network-protection mechanisms.

Pecan sales FAQ and objection responses: Integration concerns -- 'We very likely have connectors built for your platforms, but we would also be happy to build a new connector if needed.' Data concerns -- 2+ years preferred for MMM and Demand Forecasting, 10,000+ customers preferred for LTV/Churn including both churned and non-churned. Does Pecan only build one model -- No, charges per use case and iterates over time, ML models retrained as necessary. Does Pecan go away after building -- No, remains in active partnership with all managed services clients. Does Pecan implement marketing strategies -- No, provides predictions and intelligence, client acts on predictions. How many clients -- approximately 100 managed services customers. Expected KPI improvement -- 10-30% with previous clients, depends on data quality. How long to build a model -- most teams spin up first model in under a day, often hours, iterations in minutes. Do I need coding or ML skills -- No, if you can ask a clear question you are qualified. Is there a trial -- every plan is commitment-free, cancel anytime. How fast ROI -- customers often report measurable revenue lift or cost savings within first quarter.

Pecan campaign frameworks: Campaign A (Dell Technologies Capital Portfolio) -- target DTC-backed startups in AI, SaaS, analytics at Series A-D stage, credibility angle: 'We're backed by the same investors.' Campaign B (Competitor and Customer Network Expansion) -- target competitors and similar companies to existing clients (Mars, Nestlé, Fiverr, BMC, CableOne), use Similar Companies search for lookalike prospects. Campaign C (CMO-Only Campaign) -- run CMO-specific outreach based on Predictive Analytics Guide, focus on predictive marketing tied to business outcomes, solving low-trust analytics (only 28% of CMOs trust their current models per GfK/CMO Council study), ROAS and MMM ROI proof. Scripting concept: scrape one-line summary of what prospect sells, create custom blurb about how Pecan can specifically help that company, open with prospect's business context, transition to specific Pecan value proposition, close with 15-minute meeting request. Bonus qualifying question: ask which data warehouse they use.

Pecan AI elevator pitch: 'Pecan AI is a predictive analytics platform that lets business teams and data analysts -- not data scientists -- build, deploy, and act on accurate machine learning predictions. Using their Predictive AI Agent, anyone who can ask a clear business question can build a production-ready model in hours. Pecan automates the entire process from data prep through deployment and ongoing model maintenance. They're backed by $117M from Insight Partners and Google Ventures, work with approximately 100 managed services clients including Johnson and Johnson, Mars, and Redis, and deliver documented 10-30% improvements in selected KPIs.' Top 5 pains Pecan solves: (1) Cannot afford or find data scientists -- Pecan eliminates the need, starts at $760/month. (2) AI projects take months and never make it to production -- first models in hours/days with automated deployment. (3) Making decisions based on gut feel not data -- forward-looking predictions not backward-looking dashboards. (4) Don't know which customers are about to churn or which campaigns will perform -- churn/LTV/ROAS use cases. (5) Data is messy and siloed -- connects to existing sources, automates data prep, prefers messy data.

Pecan documented gaps for BDR awareness: No specific office address published. Total employee count not publicly stated. Self-service vs managed services boundary not clearly documented ($760-$2,000/month self-service vs $6-8K/month managed services handoff unclear). Managed services onboarding timeline not explicitly stated (CMO Guide mentions 'predictions within a few weeks'). Managed services contract terms (minimums, duration) not specified. No detailed case studies organized by industry vertical. Competitor comparison pages (Pecan vs SageMaker, Pecan vs Vertex AI) not fully analyzed. Enterprise tier details custom/not specified. Do not fabricate answers to questions about these gaps -- use bridge: 'That is a great question, let me connect you with our team for the specifics on that.'
